newsitem.title: UK: Hillsdown decides against "food only" route.
newsitem.headline: Hillsdown decides against "food only" route.

text.p: Diversified British food group Hillsdown Holdings Plc said on Thursday it would keep its non-food interests and use improved financial techniques to boost shareholder value across the spread of its businesses.
Hillsdown has faced pressure from shareholders in the past to sell its Fairview New Homes housebuilding business, but chief executive George Greener said the company did not plan to divest it.

He told the company's annual results conference that Fairview would stay. He said he believed the business was manageable and had not shown itself vulnerable to the cyclical nature of the housing market.

Greener, who took over as chief executive about eight months ago, has been reviewing the group's businesses and has identified those which are in strong market positions and those which are less strong.
But the group aims to manage the entire range using economic profit valuation to improve performance, he said.

Food manufacturing analysts said they were not surprised by the decision to keep Fairview. "It was already clear the corporate strategy was not to go the food-only route," said one analyst, who asked not to be identified.
Analysts said the outlook for the group was positive after the company made reasonably encouraging noises about the current year.
Earlier the company reported a 10.5 percent increase in pre-tax profits to 150.5 million pounds. The shares were up 1.5 pence at 192.5 by 1505 GMT.
